transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-01-17
Time: 09:30 PST / 17:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonas Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Helmstead Eng Mgr), Marco Silva (Helmstead Platform), Dana Ibarra (Helmstead Security)

Summary:
Helmstead is evaluating Redwood for a mixed deployment: hosted API for low-risk public-facing features, dedicated reserved capacity for high-throughput batch inference, and a private on-prem gateway for PII workloads. Main concerns: SDK integration with LangChain/LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy pattern for internal routing, rate limits/quotas across teams, and observability hooks to tie into their existing Splunk/Tempo stack.

Topics covered:
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
- LangChain and LlamaIndex adapter strategy and examples
- Gateway/onramp proxy pattern and sidecar options
- Rate limiting, per-tenant quotas, burst capacity and billing implications
- Observability integrations: webhooks, traces, token-level cost breakdowns
- Security: SOC2/ISO, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML

Transcript:
[00:00] Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, um this is Maya from Redwood, I think we all have intros but quick round robin?
[00:10] Speaker 2 (Priya): Yeah hi, Priya here, engineering manager for the conversational team at Helmstead, we own the chat flows and some internal summarization pipelines.
[00:15] Speaker 3 (Marco): Marco, platform eng, I handle infra and deployment patterns.
[00:20] Speaker 4 (Dana): Dana, security lead, I'll focus on compliance questions.
[00:24] Speaker 1 (Maya): Great. Jonas will jump in on the technical bits. Jonas, quick intro?
[00:27] Speaker 5 (Jonas): Hey team, I'm Jonas, solutions engineer, I usually do SDKs, integrations and perf work. Happy to show code later.
[00:33] Speaker 2 (Priya): Cool. Our primary ask is to figure out how Redwood fits into a mixed model. We have privacy-sensitive docs that must stay on-prem, and general consumer features where we can use hosted. Also cost is a big thing.
[00:45] Speaker 1 (Maya): Totally. At a high level you can mix hosted, dedicated and private. You can route by policy, so low-cost hosted for non-sensitive, dedicated reserved pool for predictable throughput, private on-prem for PII. We have fallbacks if dedicated is constrained.
[00:59] Speaker 3 (Marco): When you say route by policy, is that via a gateway that we run? Or is it hosted routing? We're trying to avoid lots of custom logic in our API layer.
[01:10] Speaker 5 (Jonas): Good question. We offer a lightweight onramp proxy — you can run it as a sidecar or as a centralized gateway. It supports routing rules, header-based tenant routing, and can forward to hosted or to a private Redwood control plane in your VPC. There's also a kube helm chart.
[01:28] Speaker 3 (Marco): Helm chart sounds good, do you have an example values file?
[01:32] Speaker 5 (Jonas): I can share the helm sample and a minimal values.yaml, yes. Will attach in the follow up.
[01:36] Speaker 4 (Dana): For private deployments, what's the auth model? We need SAML SSO and our KMS for key wrapping.
[01:44] Speaker 1 (Maya): On Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM, support SAML for SSO and RBAC can be mapped to groups. We'll share a compliance packet; I've got SOC2 docs ready.
[01:53] Speaker 2 (Priya): Ok good. On the integration side, our stack uses LangChain for orchestration and LlamaIndex for retrieval augmentation. How opinionated is your SDK, and do you provide first-class adapters?
[02:04] Speaker 5 (Jonas): We have language SDKs (Python/Node) and several community adapters. For LangChain, we have a Redwood LLM wrapper that implements the LLM interface — it supports streaming, function-calling and token-level cost metadata. For LlamaIndex, we have a connector pattern you can use to call Redwood endpoints for embed + query. I will share a repo snippet.
[02:22] Speaker 2 (Priya): Are there any known quirks — e.g., how the KV cache interacts with LangChain chains and when to reuse contexts?
[02:29] Speaker 5 (Jonas): The runtime manages KV cache for generation state; if you're doing lots of short-turn chat, prefix caching saves tokens. There was, um, one thing to watch: very long retriever contexts can push you into different kernel paths which affect latency; we call those out in perf profiles.
[02:45] Speaker 3 (Marco): Latency is huge. For our interactive flows we need 95th percentile < 250ms for short prompts. Can Redwood guarantee that with hosted or do we need dedicated?
[02:55] Speaker 1 (Maya): Hosted offers good latency for typical internet paths but dedicated reserved capacity is the way to get predictable P95/P99 SLAs. We can size a dedicated pool and provide SLOs. For sub-250ms you need right GPU class and model variant — we'll recommend quantized variants or smaller models for fast flows.
[03:12] Speaker 2 (Priya): And cost — how do quotas and rate limits work with multi-team tenants? We have dev/staging/prod and want per-team quotas plus burst for experiments.
[03:24] Speaker 5 (Jonas): Policy engine supports per-api-key quotas and per-tenant rate limiting; you can set steady-state QPS and a burst capacity. Billing maps to token usage per API key, and we can export token-level cost breakdowns. There's also a metering webhook for billing exports.
[03:40] Speaker 3 (Marco): If we set a conservative steady limit but allow burst, how do you handle degradations? Do requests queue at the gateway or fail fast?
[03:49] Speaker 5 (Jonas): Gateway can queue for a short window and will reject beyond that. We also support automatic fallback policies: if dedicated pool is saturated, route to hosted model variants with lower cost/latency or return a graceful degrade response.
[04:02] Speaker 4 (Dana): From a security audit POV, we need audit logs for every inference call, and the ability to retain logs for six months. What's retention and how does it work with private?
[04:12] Speaker 1 (Maya): We can route audit logs into your SIEM (Splunk) via secure forwarding for Private. Hosted retains logs per plan; for enterprise we provide configurable retention and can ship log exports. We'll include specifics in the compliance packet.
[04:25] Speaker 2 (Priya): Observability hooks — we use Tempo for traces and Prometheus for metrics. Can we get per-route latency, token breakdown, and trace spans that attach to our request ids?
[04:36] Speaker 5 (Jonas): Yes — tracers support open telemetry. We emit spans with request id and model variant metadata. Metrics include per-route token consumption, latencies and failed calls. You can also register a webhook for token-level billing events.
[04:49] Speaker 3 (Marco): Nice. About LangChain — do you support streaming responses into chains and partial outputs? We stream to client UI during generation.
[04:58] Speaker 5 (Jonas): Streaming supported in SDK and via server-sent events. The LangChain wrapper implements a streaming callback handler so you get tokens as they arrive. For LlamaIndex, we'd recommend using incremental document retrievers to keep context smaller.
[05:12] Speaker 2 (Priya): Any gotchas with LlamaIndex embeddings? We sometimes see duplicate embedding calls from our pipeline that spike costs.
[05:20] Speaker 5 (Jonas): We recommend an embedding cache layer and batch embedding endpoints — Redwood supports batch embed calls and an embedding cache TTL. We'll share best practices doc.
[05:30] Speaker 4 (Dana): About on-prem: encryption at rest and in transit, plus key management. If we want customer-managed key rotation, is that supported?
[05:39] Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes for Private you bring your KMS, we support rotation and key wrapping. We'll include KMS integration notes.
[05:46] Speaker 2 (Priya): For our pilot we'd like to test: 1) a Hosted flow for new consumer chat, 2) Dedicated reserved pool for high-throughput batch summarization, and 3) a Private onramp for PII processing. How long to spin up a dedicated pool?
[05:58] Speaker 5 (Jonas): Typical turnaround is a few days for a dev sandbox, and a week for production-grade dedicated pools depending on capacity. For private we need network setup — that can take 2-4 weeks depending on your security review.
[06:10] Speaker 3 (Marco): Can we run the onramp inside our VPC in front of Redwood hosted, so traffic never leaves our VPC for PII?
[06:17] Speaker 1 (Maya): The onramp can run in your VPC and will route to a private control plane if you provision one; if you're calling hosted endpoints, data will traverse out unless you route to private. We can show architectures for both patterns.
[06:29] Speaker 2 (Priya): Pricing question — where do quotas turn into billable overages? We want predictable billing for experiments.
[06:37] Speaker 1 (Maya): Billing is token-based; quotas enforce limits but overages can be configured to either be blocked or allowed with surcharge. For pilots we recommend hard caps and alerts to avoid surprises.
[06:48] Speaker 4 (Dana): Any regulatory constraints for EU data residency? We have offices in EU and need logs and model outputs kept in-region for some datasets.
[06:57] Speaker 5 (Jonas): Region pinning supported — you can pin workloads to a region and we provide data residency controls for logs and storage on Private or Dedicated.
[07:07] Speaker 2 (Priya): In terms of code examples, we'd like a LangChain example that shows: retrieval -> LlamaIndex -> Redwood streaming generation -> observability spans attached.
[07:16] Speaker 5 (Jonas): I'll send a minimal end-to-end example; it uses our Python SDK, LangChain adapter, and a small wrapper to forward OpenTelemetry headers.
[07:25] Speaker 3 (Marco): For performance runs, what artifact do you need from us? RPS, payload sizes, typical context length?
[07:31] Speaker 5 (Jonas): Exactly that — QPS, percentiles for context size, typical prompt/response token counts, preferred models, and an example traffic replay if possible. That lets us size the dedicated pool and recommend model variants.
[07:44] Speaker 2 (Priya): Okay we'll prepare a traffic dump.
[07:47] Speaker 4 (Dana): One last question on attestations — do you provide contract language for data handling and a DPA?
[07:53] Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, we'll include a DPA and standard SOC2 addenda in the packet.
[07:58] Speaker 2 (Priya): Great.
[08:00] Speaker 1 (Maya): To recap and next steps: I'll send compliance and pricing, Jonas will share LangChain/LlamaIndex examples plus helm values and observability webhook examples. Marco will send traffic patterns and SLOs. Then we'll schedule a bench run.
[08:16] Speaker 2 (Priya): Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:19] Speaker 3 (Marco): Thanks.
[08:20] Speaker 5 (Jonas): Thanks, talk soon.
